title: Bitwise XOR of All Pairings
statement: You get two arrays of non-negative integers, `nums1` and `nums2`. Imagine combining every element of `nums1` with every element of `nums2` (each pair of positions used once) by taking their bitwise XOR; this produces `nums1.length * nums2.length` values. Return the bitwise XOR of all of those values.
notes:
## Intuition

The brute force builds all `m * n` pairings and XORs them, which is O(m · n). XOR is order-free and `x ^ x = 0`, so all that matters is how many times each original number shows up. Every element of `nums1` takes part in exactly `nums2.length` pairings, and every element of `nums2` in exactly `nums1.length`. A number that appears an even number of times cancels out; one that appears an odd number of times survives once.

## Approach

1. Start `result` at `0`.
2. If `nums2.length` is odd, each `num` of `nums1` survives: XOR all of them into `result`.
3. If `nums1.length` is odd, each `num` of `nums2` survives: XOR all of them into `result`.
4. Return `result`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums1 = [2, 1, 3]` (length 3), `nums2 = [10, 2, 5, 0]` (length 4).

- `nums2.length = 4` is even, so the elements of `nums1` cancel and are skipped.
- `nums1.length = 3` is odd, so XOR the elements of `nums2`: `0 ^ 10 = 10`, `10 ^ 2 = 8`, `8 ^ 5 = 13`, `13 ^ 0 = 13`.
- `result = 13`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(m + n): each array is scanned at most once.
- Space: O(1): only `result` is kept.

## Pitfalls

- The parity that decides `nums1` is the length of `nums2`, and the other way round; swapping them gives wrong answers whenever exactly one length is odd.
- Building the pairings explicitly needs up to 10^10 operations at full size.
- When both lengths are even the answer is `0`, no matter what the values are.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `result` | XOR of every number that appears an odd number of times |
| `num` | the current element being folded into `result` |

narration.2: Start from 0, the value that leaves any XOR unchanged.
narration.3: Each element of nums1 is paired nums2.length times; it survives only if that count is odd.
narration.5: Fold it into the running XOR.
narration.8: Each element of nums2 is paired nums1.length times; check whether that count is odd.
narration.10: Fold it into the running XOR.
narration.13: Everything that appears an even number of times has cancelled; return what is left.
